*asterisk: properties prefixed with asterisks below are not in the specification, but serve to describe/explain it.

id.*defn: universally unique identifier (UUID) for the Composition object. Occasionally, for ease of reference, we impose an id on a Composition object, rather than generate one.

idAccount.*defn: private (to MAIA, Inc.) UUID for the user who created the new Composition object.

idEntity.*defn: public UUID for the user who created the new Composition object.

idFork.*defn: UUID for the Composition object from which the current Composition object was forked.

stampCreate.*defn: Coordinated Universal Time (UTC) for when the new Composition object was created.

stampKick.*defn: UTC for when the Composition object ceased to be available to any user.

name.*defn: display-friendly title of the loop/song/piece/composition (hereafter composition).

remarks.*defn: one or more remarks about the Composition object.

copyright.*defn: contains information about the individuals/organisations who have or are associated with copyright of the musical composition. Each element of copyright is an object with the following properties.

name.*defn: alphabetically oriented reference to the individual/organization.

composers.*defn: contains information about the individuals/organisations who composed the music. Each element of composers is an object with the same properties as copyright (see above).

lyricists.*defn: contains information about the individuals/organisations who wrote lyrics for the music. Each element of lyricists is an object with the same properties as copyright (see above).

metadata.*defn: contains information about the individuals/organisations who wrote lyrics for the music. Each element of lyricists is an object with the same properties as copyright (see above).

musicBrainz.*defn: MusicBrainz (https://musicbrainz.org/) is an open music encyclopedia that collects music metadata and makes it available to the public. For Composition objects, we like to refer to the following MusicBrainz identifiers where possible.

idArtist.*defn: UUID to the artist associated with a Composition object. Appending it to 'https://musicbrainz.org/artist/' will bring up the corresponding page.

idWork.*defn: UUID to the work corresponding to a Composition object. Appending it to 'https://musicbrainz.org/work/' will bring up the corresponding page.

wikipedia.*defn: Wikipedia (https://www.wikipedia.org/) is a free online encyclopedia, created and edited by volunteers around the world and hosted by the Wikimedia Foundation. For Composition objects, we like to refer to the following Wikipedia Uniform Resource Locators (URL) where possible.

idArtist.*defn: id for artist associated with a Composition object. Appending it to 'https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/' will bring up the corresponding page.

idLyricist.*defn: id for lyricist associated with a Composition object. Appending it to 'https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/' will bring up the corresponding page.

idPiece.*defn: id for piece corresponding to a Composition object. Appending it to 'https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/' will bring up the corresponding page.

imslp.*defn: The International Music Score Library Project (IMSLP, http://imslp.org/) aims to provide music scores free of charge to anyone who has internet access. For Composition objects, we like to refer to the following IMSLP URLs where possible.

idArtist.*defn: id for artist associated with a Composition object. Appending it to 'http://imslp.org/wiki/' will bring up the corresponding page.

notes.*defn: contains the note or sound events belonging to a composition. Each element of notes is an object with the following properties.

idEntity.*defn: public UUID for the user who created the new note object.

idFork.*defn: UUID for the note object from which the current note object was forked.

stampCreate.*defn: UTC for when the new note object was created.

stampKick.*defn: UTC for when the new note object ceased to be available to any user.

ontime.*defn: time measured in crotchet (quarter-note) beats at which a note begins, as displayed in piano roll (hereafter Roll) and staff notation (e.g., VexFlow).

duration.*defn: time measured in crotchet (quarter-note) beats for which a note lasts, as displayed in the Roll and staff notation.

offtime.*defn: offtime = ontime + duration. Storing it is redundant (it could be calculated on demand instead), but it is so useful that we do store it at present.

ontimeAdj.*defn: time measured in crotchet (quarter-note) beats by which the ontime of the note's playback should be adjusted. Stands for 'ontime adjusted'. This does not affect the display of the note in the Roll or staff notation, but does permit small-scale control over playback timings if the user so desires.

offtimeAdj.*defn: time measured in crotchet (quarter-note) beats by which the offtime of the note's playback should be adjusted. Comments analogous to those for ontimeAdj apply here.

pitch.*def: such as 'C#4' consisting of three components: a pitch class (one of the letters A-G); none, one, or more accidentals (# for sharp, b for flat, ## for double sharp, bb for double flat, potentially triple sharps and flats etc., but we will not cater for triple+ sharps/flats until there is a clear need); an octave number (an integer between 0 and 8, and we will not cater for outside of 'A0' to 'C8' until there is a clear need).

MNN.*def:: MIDI note number, typically between 21 and 108, corresponds to the piano key that ought to be played in order to articulate the note. Controls the vertical position of the note in the Roll. Letting f be frequency in hertz and m be MNN, the conversion formulae for equal-temperament tuning are f = 440*2^[(m - 69)/12] and m = 12*log2(f/440) + 69.

MPN.*def: morphetic pitch number, between 37 and 88, corresponds to the height of the note in staff notation, with 'C4' set arbitrarily to MPN 60. There is a bijection between pitch and (MNN, MPN), so redundancy in storing all three. For more details, see Meredith, D. (2006). The ps13 pitch spelling algorithm. Journal of New Music Research, 35(2), 121-159.

frequency.*def: cycles per second (unit Hz) at which the fundamental frequency of the note oscillates. There are conversion formulae between fundamental frequency and MNN for equal-temperament tuning, but giving users access to a frequency property enables the possibility of microtonal tuning.

barOn.*def: bar (measure) number where the note begins. If the composition has an anacrusis, notes in the anacrusis have barOn = 0.

beatOn.*def: beat of the bar where the note begins, measured in crotchets (quarter-notes). If you have timeSignatures and ontime, then you can calculate barOn and beatOn, so these are two properties that we could avoid storing, and calculate them on demand instead.

barOff.*def: bar (measure) number where the note ends. (Clarification: if a note lasts for a semibreve (whole note) in 4-4 time and has barOn = 1, then it has barOff = 2, because bar 2 beat 1 is the first instant in the music where the note no longer sounds.)

beatOff.*def: beat of the bar where the note ends, measured in crotchets (quarter-notes). If you have timeSignatures and offtime, then you can calculate barOff and beatOff, so these are two properties that we could avoid storing, and calculate them on demand instead.

staffNo.*def: index into a member of the layers array that has this same staffNo property. This property supports the association between notes and staves (e.g., for VexFlow rendering) and between notes and instruments (e.g., for Tone.js playback).

lyric.*defn: controls use of lyrics (words) associated with notes in staff notation. Each member of a lyric array is an object with the following properties.

number.*def: refers to the verse with which a particular lyric is associated (default value of 1), thus supporting multi-verse lyric rendering if required.

syllabic.*def: takes the value 'single', 'begin', 'middle', or 'end'. This is useful for rendering multi-syllable words with appropriate hyphens, for instance 'char- ac- ters', and/or for rendering melismatic material (multiple notes set to one syllable), for instance 'char- - - ac- ters'. It is also useful for reconstructing readable text from lyric arrays.

text.*def: contains the word or part-word associated with a particular note.

tie.*defn: contains quasi-notes ('quasi' in the sense that they can have all the properties that a regular note can, except 'tie') whose durations can be used to control how the parent note should be split up and then tied within or across one or more bars of music. If a note's duration is such that it extends beyond one bar but 'tie' is undefined, then staff notation-rendering code ought to populate it automatically. Each member of a tie array is an object with some of the following properties in addition to those of a regular note.

tieType.*def: takes the value 'start', 'stop', or 'stop and start', indicating whether the tie starts or stops at this note.

tieDetails.*def: contains properties for detailed management of tie appearance. An array is necessary for notes that tie over a system or page break. Each element of tieDetails is an object with some of the following properties.

firstXShift.*defn: controls horizontal start point of the tie.

lastXShift.*defn: controls horizontal stop point of the tie.

yShift.*defn: controls vertical location of the tie.

curvePoint1.*defn: sign determines upward or downward direction of the tie curve, and magnitude determines its eccentricity. If the stem of the second note is up, positive values of curvePoint1 result in downward-curving ties, and negative values in upward-curving ties. If the stem of the second note is down, positive values of curvePoint1 result in upward-curving ties, and negative values in downward-curving ties.

curvePoint2.*defn: similar to curvePoint1. Provides a second handle on eccentricity.

text.*defn: text to display above or below the tie.

font.*defn: contains properties controlling the appearance of tie text.

vexflow.*defn: contains properties that are specific to VexFlow rendering of staff notation, although they may be of use elsewhere.

voiceNo.*defn: takes the value 0, 1, 2, or 3. Enumerates independent voices that are to be displayed on one staff.

timeMod.*defn: controls the display of tuplets in staff notation.

actualNotes.*defn: a typical value for actualNotes is 3, and for normalNotes 2, which would mean that the note is notated using a notehead-stem combination worth 3/2 times the value of duration.

stem.*defn: takes the value 'up', 'down', or 'none'. Indicates whether the stem of a note goes up ('up') or down ('down'). Stemless notes are  certainly an option ('none') but not implemented in the renderer at present.

beam.*defn: controls the beaming of the note in staff notation. Beams join together notes with tails, for ease of reading and aesthetic purposes.

number.*defn: refers to a particular tail on a multi-tailed note.

type.*defn: takes the value 'begin', 'continue', or 'end'. Indicates whether the beam begins, continues, or ends on this particular note.

notehead.*defn: takes the value 'ellipse', 'cross', 'triangle', 'or 'diamond'. Indicates notehead shape used to display a note. By default, a notehead has an elliptical shape ('ellipse'), but it is possible, especially in percussion parts, to have crossed ('cross'), triangular ('triangle'), or diamond ('diamond') noteheads. Not implemented in the renderer at present (assumes 'ellipse').

accidental.*defn: takes the value Takes the value 'natural', 'sharp', 'flat', 'double sharp', or 'double flat'. indicates whether one or more sharp (♯), flat (♭) or natural (♮) signs ought to be added to the rendered note. If the property is undefined (default), no accidental sign is rendered. At present, the renderer looks for this property and ignores any accidentals in the note's pitch property.

type.*defn: takes the value 'whole', 'half', 'quarter', 'eighth', 'sixteenth', 'thirty-second', 'sixty-fourth', 'hundred and twenty-eight'. Follows the US naming tradition and can control the type of note rendered in staff notation. At present, if the property is undefined (default), the renderer infers type from the note's duration and timeMod properties.

notations.*defn: controls appearance of more staff-notation-specific properties.

techincal.*defn: controls appearance of string and fret numbers in guitar tablature, and also for the bowing direction of bowed string instruments.

string.*defn: six (6) indicates the lowest-sounding string on a six-string guitar and 1 the highest.

fret.*defn: indicates the fret on the string that ought to be pressed in order to articulate the notated pitch. Common string values are 'p', 'h', 'x', and 'b', which indicate pull-off, hammer-on, muted note, and bend, respectively.

bow.*defn: takes the value 'up' or 'down'. Indicates bow direction for a bowed string instrument.

slur.*defn: controls the positioning of slurs (or phrase marks) in staff notation. These help performers group notes together, either conceptually or more practically in terms of breathing/bowing. Visually, slurs appear very similar to ties, but musically they have a different function. Each member of a slur array is an object with the following properties.

number.*defn: refers to a particular slur attaching to a multi-slurred note. Given the definition of a slur, it is questionable why a note could have multiple slurs attached, but there are examples of this in staff notation.

type.*defn: takes the value 'start' or 'stop'. Indicates whether the slur attaches away from or toward the note.

articulations.*defn: controls placement of symbols above or below a note, indicating that it is to be articulated in a certain manner.

staccato.*defn: controls appearance of a staccato (detached) articulation.

code.*defn: each articulation glyph has an associated default string, which can be overridden.

shiftRight.*defn: shift the articulation glyph right by a specified amount.

shiftUp.*defn: shift the articulation glyph up by a specified amount.

shiftDown.*defn: shift the articulation glyph down by a specified amount. Not sure how this interacts with shiftUp.

betweenLines.*defn: indicates whether it is possible for this articulation glyph to appear between staff lines.

setPosition.*defn: not sure how this interacts with shiftUp, shiftDown, and betweenLines.

staccatissimo.*defn: controls appearance of a staccatissimo (very detached) articulation. See staccato above for properties.

accent.*defn: controls appearance of an accented articulation. See staccato above for properties.

tenuto.*defn: controls appearance of a tenuto (full-length or slightly more) articulation. See staccato above for properties.

marcato.*defn: controls appearance of a marcato (emphasized) articulation. See staccato above for properties.

pizzicatoLH.*defn: controls appearance of a left-hand pizzicato (plucked) articulation. See staccato above for properties.

pizzicatoSnap.*defn: controls appearance of a snap pizzicato (plucked so strong that the string rebounds off the fingerboard) articulation. See staccato above for properties.

naturalHarmonic.*defn: controls appearance of a natural harmonic articulation. See staccato above for properties.

fermataUpright.*defn: controls appearance of an upright fermata (pause) articulation. See staccato above for properties.

fermataInverted.*defn: controls appearance of an up-bow articulation. See staccato above for properties.

bowUp.*defn: controls appearance of a down-bow articulation. See staccato above for properties.

choked.*defn: controls appearance of a choked articulation. See staccato above for properties.

intDur.*defn: appears in a Composition object imported from a MusicXML file. Otherwise it is not important/necessary. (MusicXML requires that a composition's notes have integer durations. Each time a new note is drawn in a MusicXML file, a check determines if this note's duration is a new minimum, and if so the intDur values of all existing notes needs to be recalculated.)

tonejs.*defn: holds note properties that are specific to Tone.js playback of a composition.

idInstrument.*defn: points to a Tone.js instrument with which the note will be played back. This property enables instrument to be controlled on a note-by-note basis, but for many users this constitutes an unnecessary level of control. Not implemented in playback at present.

velocity.*defn: in [0, 1], indicates loudness with which the note is played back. This property enables velocity to be controlled on a note-by-note basis, but for many users this constitutes an unnecessary level of control.

layer.*defn: contains groupings of events (e.g., notes) into musically meaningful collections. In staff notation, for instance, a layer might be the staff to which certain notes belong. In collaborative work, this might be a user with which  certain events are associated. Each element of layer is an object with some of the following properties.

type.*defn: takes the value 'instrument' if this is a layer for associating notes with a particular staff; takes the value 'user' if this is a layer for associating events with a specific user; takes the value 'annotation' if this is a label for a collection of events.

staffNo.*defn: index for linking notes, rests, and other events to a certain staff. It is not a mandatory property of a layer, since there are other ways to link/group notes/events, but we envisage staffNo being a well-used one.

idInstrument.*defn: points to an 'instrument' with which notes belonging to this staff will be played back.

vexflow.*defn: contains properties that are specific to VexFlow rendering of staff notation, although they may be of use elsewhere.

name.*defn: display-friendly full name of the instrument/performer etc. associated with this staff.

abbreviation.*defn: display-friendly short name of the instrument/performer. In staff notation, typically the full name (our 'name' property) would be written to the left of the staff on the first system, and the abbreviated name (our 'abbreviation' property) would appear to the left of the staff on all subsequent systems.

hidden.*defn: indicates whether this staff and any events appearing on it should be rendered. Assumed true if undefined.

clef.*defn: name for the symbol plus any octave modification that will be drawn on the staff. This property is documented more fully under clefChanges (below).

clefSign.*defn: denoting the name for the symbol that will be drawn on the staff.

clefLine.*defn: indicates the staff line (counting from 1 for the bottom line) at which the drawing of the clef begins.

clefOctaveChange.*defn: indicates if the clef is altered so that everything on the clef sounds an octave or two higher/lower than indicated.

connector.*defn: indicates that a line is drawn between this staff and a subsequent staff in the notation.

name.*defn: as in vexflow property for 'name'. E.g., if a connector connects staves 3 and 4, then this name will be displayed in the staff notation halfway between the two stave, rather than labelling staves 3 and 4 separately.

toStaffNo.*defn: indicates the staffNo to which the connector is drawn.

type.*defn: takes the value 'brace' (typical for piano right- and left-hand staves), 'bracket' (typical for string quartets or orchestral sections), or 'none' (can affect the positioning of name and abbreviation without drawing a connecting line).

displayTablature.*defn: takes values 'no', 'as well', or 'only'. Specifies whether events belonging to this staff should be notated on the conventional five-line staff ('no'), on the n-line tablature staff as well ('as well'), on the n-line tablature staff only ('only'). Tablature staves do not consume an extra staffIdx, but have the same staffIdx of the conventional staff to which they belong.

tuning.*defn: contains pitch strings (such as ['E2', 'A2', 'D3', 'G3', 'B3', 'E4']). If tablature is displayed, the tuning variable controls how many strings appear (tuning.length), and the pitches in the array are the pitches of each open string (0th entry for lowest on the page).

tonejs.*defn: contains layer properties that are specific to Tone.js playback of a composition, although they may be of use elsewhere.

volume.*defn: indicates the loudness in dB with which notes belonging to this staff will be played back.

transposition.*defn: contains an MNN and an MPN. For historical reasons, some instruments are notated at one pitch but sound at another. For instance, when a 'Bb clarinet' plays the notated note 'C4', a 'Bb3' comes out. In a Composition object, the transposition array for the 'Bb clarinet' would be [−2, −1], which means each note assigned to this staff would have its MNN lowered by 2 and its MPN lowered by 1, prior to playback.

tempi.*defn: contains the initial and any subsequent tempi occurring in a composition. Any given tempo (singular of tempi) applies to all staves in a composition. A tempo is meant to indicate more than just a speed of playing: it is meant to indicate the manner in which something ought to be played too, such as “Allegro furioso” (quick and furiously!). Elements in the tempi array can be used to synchronise a performance of a piece with a symbolic representation. Each element of tempi is an object with the following properties.

ontime.*defn: time measured in crotchet (quarter-note) beats at which the tempo begins.

bpm.*defn: beats per minute. As with ontime, which has units of crotchet beats, we also measure our bpms in crotchet beats per minute.

tempo.*defn: indicates in words the speed at and/or manner in which something ought to be played.

keySignatures.*defn: contains the key signatures belonging to a composition. Unlike timeSignatures (see below), different key signatures can apply to different staves in a composition (e.g., common with transposing instruments). Each element of keySignatures is an object with the following properties.

barNo.*defn: bar (measure) where the key signature begins.

fifthSteps.*defn: indicates steps clockwise (positive) or counterclockwise (negative) from pitch-class C on the circle of fifths.

mode.*defn: in [0, 6]. Indicates a mode associated with the key signature. The major (mode 0) and minor (mode 5) modes are prevalent in Western music, but historically these were called Ionian and Aeolian respectively and were two of the seven modes: Ionian, Dorian, Phrygian, Lydian, Mixolydian, Aeolian, Locrian.

staffNo.*defn: index into the layer array, indicating the staff number on which the key signature occurs.

ontime.*defn: time measured in crotchet beats at which the key signature begins.

timeSignatures.*defn: contains the time signatures belonging to a composition. We assume (for the time being at least) that any given time signature applies to all staves in a composition. Each element of timeSignatures is an object with the following properties.

barNo.*defn: bar (measure) where the time signature begins.

topNo.*defn: top number in a time signature, denoting the number of beats in a bar.

bottomNo.*defn: takes the value 1, 2, 4, 8, 16, or 32. The bottom number in a time signature denotes the type of beat (1 for semibreve or whole note, 2 for minim of half note, etc.).

ontime.*defn: time measured in crotchet beats at which the time signature begins.

clefChanges.*defn: contains initial and any subsequent clefs belonging to a composition. Each element of clefChanges is an object with the following properties.

ontime.*defn: time measured in crotchet beats at which the clef begins.

clef.*defn: denotes the name for the symbol plus any octave modification that will be drawn on the staff. The values 'treble clef' and 'bass clef' are by far the most common, but the following are also possibilities: 'treble clef 8va', 'treble clef 15ma', 'treble clef 8vb', 'French violin clef', 'soprano clef', 'mezzo-soprano clef', 'alto clef', 'tenor clef', 'baritone clef (C clef)', 'bass clef 8va', 'bass clef 15ma', 'bass clef 8vb', 'bass clef 15mb', 'alto clef', 'baritone clef (F clef)', 'subbass clef 15mb', 'percussion clef', or 'tablature'.

clefSign.*defn: denoting the name for the symbol that will be drawn on the staff.

clefLine.*defn: indicates the staff line (counting from 1 for the bottom line) at which the drawing of the clef begins.

clefOctaveChange.*defn: indicates if the clef is altered so that everything on the clef sounds an octave or two higher/lower than indicated.

staffNo.*defn: index into the layer array, indicating the staff number on which the clef occurs.

sequencing.*defn: needs further work, but will control non-linear aspects of playback, including consequences for sound and notation.

rests.*defn: needs further work, but it is in use already. Rests are not required in order for a Composition object to be rendered correctly, but they can be defined explicitly if, say, a user wants to subdivide a resting period in a specific way.

pageLayout.*defn: needs further work, but it is in use already. Contains things like page and system breaks.

miscXML.*defn: needs further work, but contains miscellaneous information from a MusicXML import. It also contains the divisions value as well as information about whether the incoming sheet music has an anacrusis.
